records.environment: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest (CI run 44352965914); reproduction in a clean ubuntu:24.04 container with host networking
records.summary: CI run 1 failed in the tool bootstrap; root cause fixed and verified in a clean container
records.steps: Read the failed job log; reproduced with an empty download cache in ubuntu:24.04; patched tools/bootstrap/install-dev-tools.sh; re-ran install, an idempotent second run, and a negative run with downloads blocked.
records.observed: Root cause: log() printed to stdout inside fetch(), whose stdout is captured as the file path; with a cold cache the log line corrupted the tar path. tar && install masked the failure under set -e, so the script falsely reported 'installed' and exited 0 (actionlint: command not found at the next step). Fix: messages to stderr, shopt -s inherit_errexit, separate tar and install steps, verify_installed after each tool, explicit download failure. After the fix: all three tools install with their versions verified; re-run reports 'present'; blocked downloads exit 1 with 'download failed'. Local runs had passed only because the cache was warm.

records.summary: Database policy suite: 108 pgTAP assertions pass on the local Supabase stack (Postgres 17.12)
records.steps: pnpm db:reset; pnpm db:test (supabase test db runs pg_prove over supabase/tests/01-04_*.test.sql); then each file again with psql on a database already populated by end-to-end runs
records.observed: Files=4, Tests=108, Result: PASS, also on the populated database. Covers: table and column grants, RLS on every table, no views, pinned search_path on definer functions, desk_app without privileges (AT-25); readers, unassigned, disabled and revoked staff see nothing (AT-03); agents cannot update items or insert proposals that look reviewed (AT-04); agents have no access to pitches, rights or the sources table and read sources only through SQL-side redaction (AT-06); a revoked agent is denied while another authenticates, revocation is final and revokes its tokens (AT-07); a duplicate idempotency key is rejected by the database (AT-12/AT-13 database layer); intake throttling, disposition, sequential content IDs, derived deciders and reviewers, and the append-only audit trail with request IDs.

records.summary: Mutation test of the policy suite: all 11 deliberate breaks are caught by named assertions
records.steps: For each mutation, inside a rolled-back transaction: apply it, run every test file with psql -At and count 'not ok' lines. Baseline without a mutation: 0 failures.
records.observed: Caught: private_contact granted to desk_agent (4 assertions); agent item policy opened (3); staff pitch policy weakened to any signed-in user (5); whole-row UPDATE on pitches (2); reactivation guard dropped (1); revocation cascade dropped (1); credit-line constraint dropped (1); decider stamping dropped (1); idempotency unique constraint dropped (2); whole-row INSERT on proposals for agents (1); audit truncate guard dropped (1).

records.summary: Unit suite: 67 Vitest tests pass

records.observed: 8 files, 67 tests: the next action for every status, overdue and blocked states (SC-007); CSP, request IDs and redirect safety; trusted-proxy client addresses; agent token generation and parsing; canonical payload hashing for idempotency (AT-12/AT-13); redaction shape (AT-06); cursors; in-process rate guards; form validation; every contract example behaves as labelled, including posts.publish and members.export rejected (AT-04).

records.summary: End-to-end suite: 24 Playwright tests pass against a production build, with no axe WCAG 2.2 AA violations
records.steps: pnpm db:reset; pnpm desk:env; next build; next start; pnpm desk:e2e --trace off (Chromium desktop 1360x900 at 2x and Pixel 7); sign-in links read from the local Mailpit inbox
records.observed: 24 passed. Public pitch to decision to story with next action, Ghost link (a pasted editor URL is reduced to the ID; a second item cannot reuse it), sources, rights and the release gate (SC-006, SC-007). A reader identity and a disabled staff member are denied on the next request (AT-03, SC-005). posts.publish, members.export, a status field in draft content and a client-supplied principal are rejected (AT-04). items.read omits staff-only sources and private fields; redacted entries are explicit (AT-06). A retry returns the original draft; a changed body gets 409 and the original stays intact (AT-12, AT-13). Revoking the token in Settings denies the next request (AT-07). Hostile markup in public and agent intake renders as inert text and no file upload exists (AT-18, desk surfaces only; Ghost cards are out of scope). Security headers, nonce CSP, strict request IDs, prototype keys rejected, no horizontal overflow at phone width.

records.summary: No secrets or unnecessary private records in client bundles, gateway responses or logs
records.steps: pnpm desk:build (apps/desk/scripts/scan-bundle.mjs over .next/static and prerendered payloads), a planted-secret control, a search of the server log captured during the end-to-end run, and gateway response assertions
records.observed: 44 shipped files against 11 rules, including the literal local secret values: no findings. Control: a planted INTAKE_HASH_SECRET value and an sb_secret_ string were both detected. Server log: 51 JSON lines with request and trace IDs and no emails, tokens, keys, database URLs or private contacts (agent requests log only the token prefix). items.read responses contain no private fields. The publishable key is also absent from browser bundles.

records.summary: Independent security review of the desk: no Critical or High findings; all 3 Medium and 5 Low findings fixed and re-tested
records.steps: A separate agent reviewed the migration, data access, auth, gateway, actions and scripts adversarially, probing as an editor and as an agent in rolled-back transactions; each finding was fixed and covered by new pgTAP, unit or end-to-end assertions, then every suite was re-run
records.observed: Medium: anonymous gateway traffic wrote permanent audit rows and held shared connections (fixed: no database work without a token shape, failed-auth limit per client, 4 concurrent gateway transactions, per-agent budget in the database); intake throttle keyed on client-controlled X-Forwarded-For and racy (fixed: trusted proxy hops required in production, shared buckets otherwise, advisory lock); staff could rewrite whole rows and several changes were unaudited (fixed: column-level UPDATE grants, database-stamped reviewers and deciders, credit-line constraint, audit triggers on sources and rights, audited refusals). Low: prototype keys passed the section allow-list (Object.hasOwn and a database check); docs overstated audit coverage (corrected); raw agent request IDs stored (strict IDs); revoked agents could be reactivated (final revocation that revokes tokens); agent rules looser than the gateway (column-level INSERT grants, SQL-side source redaction, agents limited to agent.* audit events).

Google Cloud free tier: Cloud Run 2M requests, 180,000 vCPU-seconds, 360,000 GiB-seconds; Cloud Storage 5 GB-months in us-east1/us-west1/us-central1. Estimated cash total about $84-99/month against the packet's $119-169.

records.summary: Independent security review of agent publishing (v0.4.0): 1 High, 4 Medium and 3 Low findings, all fixed in v0.4.1 with regression tests, plus 8 more found while fixing
records.steps: A separate agent reviewed the publishing migration, executor, deploy, gateway, actions and local site server adversarially. Each finding was reproduced, fixed and covered by pgTAP, unit or end-to-end assertions, and every suite was re-run on the final build
records.observed: High: rebuilds used current or edited text and a hand-settable status (fixed: published_revision plus a status guard trigger). Medium: incomplete re-checks at claim; no lease fencing (possible double email or overlapping deploys); unclaimable jobs could wedge the queue; refused requests rolled back by the gateway savepoint. Low: private-contact oracle outside an open lane; entity, list-quote and link bypasses; serve-site open redirect and crash on bad escapes. Found while fixing: retries could publish a person's later edit; retries of live agent jobs were cancelled; Markdown-escape, emphasis and invisible-character bypasses of the contact check; international phone numbers; a second publish could email twice; editor-facing failure details shown to agents; accented titles made poor addresses; cancelled claims reported to agents as queued

New publishing assertions: token-fenced snapshot, mark and complete; a re-claim after lease expiry gets a new token and locks the old worker out; second email mark refused; snapshot uses published_revision after a later edit; hand status changes to and from Published refused (42501); claim cancels jobs after revocation, rejection or withdrawn email permission, with the reason; already-live retry keeps the agent's revision; publish on a live story refused; already_emailed warning; 10-refusal budget; entity, list-quote, uncited-link, escaped and emphasis-split email, international phone and emphasis-split private-contact refusals; content checks not run with the switch off; slug fallback and transliteration

records.summary: Live publishing sweep endpoint refuses every caller without a Google-signed token for its address and account; the desk on Cloud Run reaches Google's signing keys
records.steps: POST https://sc-desk-629322111689.us-west1.run.app/api/publishing/sweep with (1) no Authorization header, (2) an HS256 token with a dummy signature naming the scheduler account, (3) an RS256 token signed by a key generated locally with every claim right (issuer accounts.google.com, this exact audience, the scheduler account, email_verified, fresh); then GET on the same address; then read the desk's Cloud Run log entries "publish sweep refused"

records.summary: Red team: the v0.7.0 desk, in its own container with Cloud Run's limits, is killed by a 24-megapixel upload, and refuses uploads over 10 MB as unreadable
records.steps: docker build of c0f06c7 (git archive); docker run --memory 512m --memory-swap 512m --cpus 1 against the local stack; signed in as a local owner through Mailpit; POSTed synthetic camera-like JPEGs (12, 24, 45, 59 megapixels) to /stories/<id>/image with a cleared rights record; read the container's memory cgroup (max_usage_in_bytes, failcnt) and the server's VmHWM after each upload
records.observed: 12 MP (2.6 MB): attached in 30.9 s, server resident peak 483 MiB of 512. 24 MP (5.1 MB): the container was OOM-killed after 15 s (exit 137, OOMKilled=true), the request hung up and the desk was down. Separately, a 12.6 MB upload returned 'unreadable' in 0.1 s; the log said 'Request body exceeded 10MB ... Only the first 10MB will be available' (the Next.js proxy's default body limit). Standalone, sharp alone peaked at 385 MiB (12 MP) to 939 MiB (59 MP): every rendition was decoded from a full-size PNG intermediate

records.summary: v0.7.1 desk container under 512 MiB and one CPU: 12 to 59 megapixel uploads up to 14.4 MiB attach, one at a time and two at once, with no memory-limit hits
records.steps: Same harness as the failing run, image built from the fixed tree (master decode with shrink-on-load, 4.3-megapixel cap, one image at a time, libvips cache off, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, proxyClientMaxBodySize 16mb)
records.observed: Charged container memory peaks (server VmHWM in brackets): 12 MP 300 MiB (360) in 28.0 s; 24 MP portrait 342 (403) in 41.4 s; 45 MP 376 (436) in 19.3 s; 59 MP 12.6 MB 446 (507) in 23.4 s; 59 MP 14.4 MiB 456 (509) in 22.6 s; 24 MP and 59 MP together 391 (452), 41.6 s and 65.7 s. All HTTP 303 ?image=attached, failcnt 0, OOMKilled false, health 200, no body-limit warnings. Because the high-water mark nears 512 MiB, the service moves to 1 GiB
